sg.constructed-scenarios.coverage_claim: The handoffs drawing from the labeled ce.account_changes source that are members of this group establish this account statement's identity, effective time, and constructed label: account_id populates account_number and action_at populates effective_from, satisfying L1.identity's persistent-identity requirement and L1.history/L1.as-of's dated, ordered statement requirement for this source specifically; provenance populates the account statement's own provenance field, and only ever from this source, while no raw-sourced handoff ever populates it, satisfying L1.constructed-scenarios' 'labeled... wherever it appears' and 'never mixed into the received records.' The standing facts this source's rows also carry, status_id and tax_status_id, are populated by handoffs that are members of sg.statement-content instead, since content coverage is the more specific claim owned there; this group's coverage is limited to identity, history/as-of, and labeling for this source.

handoff.ce.account_changes.account_id->l.necessity: the account this labeled scenario is about must carry the same identity role as any received account statement; account_id is this constructed source's account number.
handoff.ce.account_changes.account_id->l.parallel_assumption: Credible while account_id in a constructed scenario names an account_number already or separately established as identity.

handoff.ce.account_changes.action_at->lo.necessity: unlike incremental CDC files, this labeled constructed source carries its own explicit moment of change (action_at), so the effective_from this job requires under L1.history and L1.as-of is directly available without resolving the change-effective-time hole.
handoff.ce.account_changes.action_at->lo.parallel_assumption: Credible while action_at records the moment the constructed scenario asserts the change takes effect.

handoff.ce.account_changes.provenance->l.necessity: the clause requires a constructed scenario be labeled wherever it appears; this source's own provenance field is the label to carry through.
handoff.ce.account_changes.provenance->l.parallel_assumption: Credible while every row from this source carries a non-empty provenance label.

inv.constructed_account_change_refers_to.necessity: L1.constructed-scenarios' authorized clarification states a constructed scenario changes something the received records already know and never introduces a customer, account, or trade the brokerage does not have; this invariant is the direct check of that requirement for ce.account_changes. It is also what guarantees that logical.account.owning_customer_number's carried_forward_from_previous_statement derivation always has a previous statement to carry from for a constructed change.
inv.constructed_account_change_refers_to.parallel_assumption: Holds while every constructed scenario used to test this job's rules is authored against an account already present in the received records, per the authorized clarification of L1.constructed-scenarios.

inv.constructed_scenarios_labeled.necessity: the clause requires constructed scenarios to be labeled wherever they appear and never mixed into received records; this invariant is the direct check of that requirement at the attribute level.
inv.constructed_scenarios_labeled.parallel_assumption: Holds as long as constructed scenarios are only ever loaded through the labeled ce.account_changes source and never through a raw source.

logical.account.provenance.necessity: the clause requires a constructed scenario be labeled wherever it appears; this attribute carries that label on the account statement so it is never mistaken for a received record.
logical.account.provenance.parallel_assumption: Credible while the only anchored constructed-scenario source for this job is account-level; no equivalent labeled source exists yet for customer statements.

type.constructed_scenario_label.necessity: the clause requires any constructed scenario be labeled wherever it appears and never mixed into received records; a dedicated provenance value is indispensable to carry that label through the model. It belongs to one dated statement and is never replaced in place, which is the per_statement mutation role.
type.constructed_scenario_label.parallel_assumption: Credible while every constructed scenario is loaded only through its labeled source and every received record is loaded only through raw sources.

sg.current-version.coverage_claim: The is_current flag, true for exactly the statement of a customer or account with no later statement and false for every other, together with the single-current invariants, is a direct restatement of L1.current-version's 'exactly one current statement per customer and per account.' This determination depends on every statement's effective_from being known; where a statement's only source is an incremental CDC file, its order relative to the customer's or account's other statements is not yet resolvable, so its current-ness cannot yet be determined either.

inv.account_single_current.necessity: L1.current-version states there is exactly one current statement per account; this invariant is the direct restatement of that requirement over the is_current flag.
inv.account_single_current.parallel_assumption: Holds as long as every statement of an account is recorded with a determinable order; two statements claiming the same effective moment would make the current one undecidable.

inv.customer_single_current.necessity: L1.current-version states there is exactly one current statement per customer; this invariant is the direct restatement of that requirement over the is_current flag.
inv.customer_single_current.parallel_assumption: Holds as long as every statement of a customer is recorded with a determinable order; two statements claiming the same effective moment would make the current one undecidable.

logical.account.is_current.necessity: L1.current-version requires exactly one current statement per account, defined as the one with no later statement; this attribute exposes that fact directly.
logical.account.is_current.parallel_assumption: Credible once every account statement has a known effective_from to order it against the others.

logical.customer.is_current.necessity: L1.current-version requires exactly one current statement per customer, defined as the one with no later statement; this attribute exposes that fact directly.
logical.customer.is_current.parallel_assumption: Credible once every customer statement has a known effective_from to order it against the others.

type.statement_is_current.necessity: L1.current-version defines the current statement as the one with no later statement and requires exactly one per customer or account; a flag recording that fact is indispensable to expose it without recomputation. It is a fact about that dated statement relative to the others, never edited in place on an existing statement, which is the per_statement mutation role, not mutable.
type.statement_is_current.parallel_assumption: Credible as long as effective moments are known and ordered for every statement of a thing; if effective moments are missing, the current flag cannot be determined either.

sg.history-asof.coverage_claim: For every statement whose source carries its own moment of change (the historical action file's action_ts), effective_from is populated and the no-overlap and unique-answer invariants hold over it, satisfying L1.history's 'kept, with the moment it took effect' and L1.as-of's 'the latest one that took effect at or before it.' The labeled constructed account scenario's own effective_from handoff (action_at) is covered under sg.constructed-scenarios instead, since it is the more specific claim about that source. Incremental CDC records carry no moment of their own (a batch date is not an effective moment, per L1.hole.change-effective-time), so no effective_from handoff is created from them.

handoff.raw.customer_mgmt_action.action_.necessity: L1.history requires the moment an account change took effect; action_ts is this file's own recorded moment for the action, unlike incremental change files which carry none of their own.
handoff.raw.customer_mgmt_action.action_.parallel_assumption: Credible while action_ts records the moment the brokerage considers the change to have taken effect, not merely when it was received into this file.

handoff.raw.customer_mgmt_action.action_.necessity: L1.history requires the moment a customer change took effect; action_ts is this file's own recorded moment for the action, unlike incremental change files which carry none of their own.
handoff.raw.customer_mgmt_action.action_.parallel_assumption: Credible while action_ts records the moment the brokerage considers the change to have taken effect, not merely when it was received into this file.

inv.account_asof_has_unique_answer.necessity: L1.as-of defines the as-of answer as the latest statement that took effect at or before the queried moment, which is unique only if statements are ordered and non-overlapping.
inv.account_asof_has_unique_answer.parallel_assumption: Holds under the no-overlap and ordering assumptions above; if they fail, an as-of question could have more than one candidate answer, which should trigger review.

inv.account_statements_no_overlap.necessity: L1.history requires a later statement to sit beside the earlier one rather than overlapping it, and L1.as-of's requirement that any as-of question have exactly one answer holds only if statements partition time without overlap; this invariant is the direct restatement of that non-overlap requirement.
inv.account_statements_no_overlap.parallel_assumption: Holds while effective_from values are strictly ordered per account; a duplicate or out-of-order effective_from would break the partition and should trigger review.

inv.customer_asof_has_unique_answer.necessity: L1.as-of defines the as-of answer as the latest statement that took effect at or before the queried moment, which is unique only if statements are ordered and non-overlapping.
inv.customer_asof_has_unique_answer.parallel_assumption: Holds under the no-overlap and ordering assumptions above; if they fail, an as-of question could have more than one candidate answer, which should trigger review.

inv.customer_statements_no_overlap.necessity: L1.history requires a later statement to sit beside the earlier one rather than overlapping it, and L1.as-of's requirement that any as-of question have exactly one answer holds only if statements partition time without overlap; this invariant is the direct restatement of that non-overlap requirement.
inv.customer_statements_no_overlap.parallel_assumption: Holds while effective_from values are strictly ordered per customer; a duplicate or out-of-order effective_from would break the partition and should trigger review.

logical.account.effective_from.necessity: L1.history requires the moment a change took effect be kept with the statement; L1.as-of requires that moment to determine which statement answers a query as of any time.
logical.account.effective_from.parallel_assumption: Credible where the source of this statement supplies its own moment of change; not yet derivable for incremental account change records.

logical.customer.effective_from.necessity: L1.history requires the moment a change took effect be kept with the statement; L1.as-of requires that moment to determine which statement answers a query as of any time.
logical.customer.effective_from.parallel_assumption: Credible where the source of this statement supplies its own moment of change; not yet derivable for incremental customer change records.

type.statement_effective_from.necessity: L1.history requires the moment a change took effect be kept beside the statement, and L1.as-of requires ordering statements by that moment to answer any as-of question; a dedicated effective-time value is indispensable to both. It belongs to one dated statement and is never replaced in place, which is exactly the per_statement mutation role.
type.statement_effective_from.parallel_assumption: Credible while every statement's effective moment can be determined at all; where a source supplies no moment of its own, this value cannot yet be assigned and as-of answers for that statement are unavailable.

sg.identity.coverage_claim: Every source this job reads through a raw feed that reports a customer or account carries its own identity handoff into the customer_number or account_number attribute, typed with the identity mutation role, giving each entity the persistent, non-identity-changing value L1.identity requires. Because a versioned entity's statements must also be kept beside one another and be orderable for as-of resolution, this group also covers the entity-shape-level portion of L1.history and L1.as-of: the historical action file's own action_ts handoff makes both entities projectable as dated, ordered statements now; the incremental CDC files carry the same identity values but supply no effective moment of their own, so their identity handoffs into these versioned entities are deferred. The labeled constructed account scenario's own identity handoff is covered under sg.constructed-scenarios instead, since it is the more specific claim about that source. L1.identity also names a trade number, out of this job's scope (see job:trade-lifecycle). The attribute-level effective_from population and ordering invariants are covered by sg.history-asof; the current-flag mechanics by sg.current-version.

handoff.raw.account_cdc.ca_id->logical.a.necessity: identity of the account a change applies to must be carried even where the change's effective moment is not yet resolvable; ca_id is this file's account number.
handoff.raw.account_cdc.ca_id->logical.a.parallel_assumption: Credible while ca_id in this file matches the same numbering as the historical load.

handoff.raw.customer_cdc.c_id->logical.c.necessity: identity of the customer a change applies to must be carried even where the change's effective moment is not yet resolvable; c_id is this file's customer number.
handoff.raw.customer_cdc.c_id->logical.c.parallel_assumption: Credible while c_id values in this file match the same numbering as the historical load.

handoff.raw.customer_mgmt_action.c_id->l.necessity: L1.identity requires the customer's own number as its identity; this file's customer actions (NEW, UPDCUST, INACT) carry c_id as the brokerage's customer number on each such record.
handoff.raw.customer_mgmt_action.c_id->l.parallel_assumption: Credible while c_id values in this file are the brokerage's real customer numbers and not reused for different customers.

handoff.raw.customer_mgmt_action.ca_id->.necessity: L1.identity requires the account's own number as its identity; this file's account actions (NEW, ADDACCT, UPDACCT, CLOSEACCT) carry ca_id as that number.
handoff.raw.customer_mgmt_action.ca_id->.parallel_assumption: Credible while ca_id values in this file are the brokerage's real account numbers.

logical.account.necessity: L1.identity, L1.history, and L1.as-of require the same versioned-and-identified shape as the customer entity: a persistent identified account with dated, kept, orderable statements. The single-current-statement requirement, the owning-customer link, and the standing facts each statement carries are further specified, at the attribute level, by L1.current-version, L1.owner-standing, and L1.statement-content respectively.
logical.account.parallel_assumption: Credible while every recorded change to an account is delivered as a new statement rather than an overwrite of a prior one.

logical.account.account_number.necessity: L1.identity requires a value that identifies which account a statement is about and stays the same across that account's changes; this attribute carries the identity type for exactly that purpose.
logical.account.account_number.parallel_assumption: Credible while the brokerage's account number is stable and unique per account.

logical.customer.necessity: L1.identity requires the customer to be a persistent identified thing rather than a row that changes identity; L1.history requires every change kept beside the earlier one with its effective moment; L1.as-of requires the kept statements be ordered so any moment resolves to one of them — together these entail a versioned entity of dated statements about one identified customer. The single-current-statement requirement and the standing facts each statement carries are further specified, at the attribute level, by L1.current-version and L1.statement-content respectively.
logical.customer.parallel_assumption: Credible while every recorded change to a customer is delivered as a new statement rather than an overwrite of a prior one.

logical.customer.customer_number.necessity: L1.identity requires a value that identifies which customer a statement is about and stays the same across that customer's changes; this attribute carries the identity type for exactly that purpose.
logical.customer.customer_number.parallel_assumption: Credible while the brokerage's customer number is stable and unique per customer.

type.account_number.necessity: L1.identity requires that a change to an account does not make it a different account; a value invariant across all of an account's dated statements is required to express that persistence, which is exactly the identity mutation role.
type.account_number.parallel_assumption: Credible while the brokerage's account number is never reassigned to a different account; if an account number were reused for a different account this role would misidentify statements, which should trigger review.

type.customer_number.necessity: L1.identity requires that a change to a customer does not make it a different customer; a value invariant across all of a customer's dated statements is required to express that persistence, which is exactly the identity mutation role.
type.customer_number.parallel_assumption: Credible while the brokerage's customer number is never reassigned to a different customer; if a customer number were reused for a different customer this role would misidentify statements, which should trigger review.

sg.owner-standing.coverage_claim: Every account statement sourced from a feed that itself supplies the account's own effective moment carries the identity of its owning customer: directly, from the historical action file's own c_id (the incremental account CDC file's own c_id handoff is deferred pending its own effective-time hole); and, for a statement sourced from the labeled constructed scenario ce.account_changes, which carries no owner field of its own, from this same attribute's own carried_forward_from_previous_statement derivation under L1.omitted-facts-stand, which holds that a constructed change not mentioning the owner leaves it as it last stood. L1.identity and L1.history make 'the account's immediately preceding statement' well defined, and L1.constructed-scenarios together with inv.constructed_account_change_refers_to_known_account guarantee that a preceding statement exists to carry from. The account_asof_carries_customer_asof invariant requires that owning-customer value be used to pair the account's as-of answer with the customer's as-of answer at the same moment — exactly L1.owner-standing's 'an account's standing includes its owner's standing,' using L1.as-of's same-moment lookup rule. L1.statement-content additionally names 'which customer owns it' as part of what an account statement carries, which this same attribute satisfies.

handoff.raw.account_cdc.c_id->logical.ac.necessity: L1.owner-standing requires the owning customer be carried on the account's statement; this incremental file's c_id supplies that value even while the statement's own effective moment is unresolved.
handoff.raw.account_cdc.c_id->logical.ac.parallel_assumption: Credible while c_id on an account change record names the customer who owns the account as of that change, independent of when the change is deemed to take effect.

handoff.raw.customer_mgmt_action.c_id->l.necessity: L1.owner-standing requires the account's statement to name the customer whose standing it includes; this file's account actions (NEW, ADDACCT, UPDACCT, CLOSEACCT) carry c_id as the owning customer at the moment of the action.
handoff.raw.customer_mgmt_action.c_id->l.parallel_assumption: Credible while an account action in this file always reports the customer who owns the account at that same moment.

inv.account_asof_carries_customer_asof.necessity: L1.owner-standing requires that an account's standing at a moment include how its customer stood at that same moment; L1.as-of supplies the same-moment lookup rule for both entities.
inv.account_asof_carries_customer_asof.parallel_assumption: Holds as long as the account's owning_customer_number is known for the statement in question; where it is not yet derivable, the paired customer as-of answer cannot be produced either.

logical.account.owning_customer_number.necessity: L1.owner-standing requires that an account's standing include its owner's standing, and L1.statement-content names 'which customer owns it' as part of what an account statement carries; this attribute names which customer that is so the customer's as-of statement can be looked up for the same moment. Where a statement's source does not supply this fact directly, this attribute's own carried_forward_from_previous_statement derivation supplies it instead, per L1.omitted-facts-stand, L1.identity, and L1.history.
logical.account.owning_customer_number.parallel_assumption: Credible for whatever account statements exist; whether a change to the customer alone produces a new account statement carrying this same value is unresolved. The carried-forward derivation is credible while a change that does not mention the owner is understood to leave the owner unchanged rather than unknown; if the business intends otherwise, this derivation must be revisited.

type.account_owner_reference.necessity: L1.owner-standing requires that an account's standing include its owner's standing, and L1.statement-content names 'which customer owns it' as part of what an account's dated statement carries; the account's statement must therefore carry which customer it belongs to so that customer's as-of statement can be found for the same moment. This value belongs to one dated statement and is never replaced in place, which is the per_statement mutation role.
type.account_owner_reference.parallel_assumption: Credible while every account statement's owning customer is knowable at the moment the statement is recorded; whether a change to the owner alone creates a new account statement is unresolved.

sg.statement-content.coverage_claim: For every customer statement sourced from the historical action file: tier is handed off directly from c_tier on NEW and UPDCUST rows, and carried forward from the customer's preceding statement under L1.omitted-facts-stand on INACT rows, which omit c_tier; status is derived from action_type on every one of NEW, UPDCUST, and INACT, since the anchored action_type_meanings state a status for each. Both standing facts L1.statement-content names for a customer are therefore populated for every statement this source produces, by direct handoff or carry-forward. For every account statement sourced from the historical action file: tax_treatment is handed off directly from ca_tax_st on NEW, ADDACCT, and UPDACCT rows, and carried forward from the account's preceding statement under L1.omitted-facts-stand on CLOSEACCT rows, which omit ca_tax_st; status is derived from action_type on every one of NEW, ADDACCT, UPDACCT, and CLOSEACCT. Both facts L1.statement-content names for an account are therefore populated for every statement this source produces; the owning-customer fact it also names is covered under sg.owner-standing instead, since it is the more specific claim about that attribute. For every account statement sourced from the labeled constructed scenario ce.account_changes — the one account source with no pending effective-time hole of its own — status and tax treatment are handed off directly from that source's own status_id and tax_status_id fields, present on every row, so this fully projectable source's statements are not content-free. The incremental CDC files carry the same tier, tax-treatment, and status values but supply no effective moment of their own, so all of their content handoffs into these versioned entities remain deferred.
sg.statement-content.gap: L1.hole.change-effective-time bounds the deferred CDC-sourced handoffs above, which cannot yet be projected. Separately, L1.hole.closed-account-activity bounds the account status this group now derives from action_type: a CLOSEACCT statement's closed status is not revised by this model if the account's activity later resumes without a recorded reopening action.

handoff.ce.account_changes.status_id->lo.necessity: L1.statement-content requires an account's dated statement to carry whether the account is open or closed; this labeled constructed source's own status_id field supplies that fact directly for scenarios built to test these rules, per L1.constructed-scenarios.
handoff.ce.account_changes.status_id->lo.parallel_assumption: Credible while status_id on a constructed account-change row states the open/closed status the scenario asserts the account holds as of that row's action_at, using the anchored status_codes (ACTV: active or open; INAC: inactive or closed).

handoff.ce.account_changes.tax_status_id.necessity: L1.statement-content requires an account's dated statement to carry its tax treatment; this labeled constructed source's own tax_status_id field supplies that value directly for scenarios built to test these rules, per L1.constructed-scenarios.
handoff.ce.account_changes.tax_status_id.parallel_assumption: Credible while tax_status_id on a constructed account-change row states the tax-treatment code the scenario asserts the account holds as of that row's action_at.

handoff.raw.account_cdc.ca_st_id->logica.necessity: L1.statement-content requires an account's dated statement to carry whether the account is open or closed; this incremental file's ca_st_id is the brokerage's own recorded status value, supplying that fact even while the statement's own effective moment is unresolved.
handoff.raw.account_cdc.ca_st_id->logica.parallel_assumption: Credible while ca_st_id on an account change record names the open/closed status the brokerage considers the account to hold as of that change.

handoff.raw.account_cdc.ca_tax_st->logic.necessity: L1.statement-content requires an account's dated statement to carry its tax treatment; this incremental file's ca_tax_st supplies that value even while the statement's own effective moment is unresolved.
handoff.raw.account_cdc.ca_tax_st->logic.parallel_assumption: Credible while ca_tax_st on an account change record names the tax treatment the brokerage considers the account to hold as of that change, independent of when the change is deemed to take effect.

handoff.raw.customer_cdc.c_st_id->logica.necessity: L1.statement-content requires a customer's dated statement to carry whether the customer is active or inactive; this incremental file's c_st_id is the brokerage's own recorded status value, supplying that fact even while the statement's own effective moment is unresolved.
handoff.raw.customer_cdc.c_st_id->logica.parallel_assumption: Credible while c_st_id on a customer change record names the active/inactive status the brokerage considers the customer to hold as of that change.

handoff.raw.customer_cdc.c_tier->logical.necessity: L1.statement-content requires a customer's dated statement to carry the customer's tier; this incremental file's c_tier supplies that value even while the statement's own effective moment is unresolved.
handoff.raw.customer_cdc.c_tier->logical.parallel_assumption: Credible while c_tier on a customer change record names the tier the brokerage considers the customer to hold as of that change, independent of when the change is deemed to take effect.

handoff.raw.customer_mgmt_action.action_.necessity: L1.history requires every change to an account be kept as a new dated statement, and this row's action_type marks exactly such a change (NEW, ADDACCT, UPDACCT, CLOSEACCT); L1.statement-content requires that statement carry whether the account is open or closed. chain/anchors/sources-v1.json states what each code means (NEW, ADDACCT, UPDACCT: open; CLOSEACCT: closed) with its own cited authority; interpreting that stated meaning to populate this statement's status is reading a named reference the source defines, not inventing a mapping from action codes to status values.
handoff.raw.customer_mgmt_action.action_.parallel_assumption: Credible while the anchored action_type_meanings correctly and exhaustively state NEW, ADDACCT, and UPDACCT as open and CLOSEACCT as closed for an account statement. Whether a CLOSEACCT statement's closed status remains accurate if the account is later found active again (activity recorded after closure with no reopening action) is bounded by L1.hole.closed-account-activity, not resolved by this handoff.

handoff.raw.customer_mgmt_action.action_.necessity: L1.history requires every change to a customer be kept as a new dated statement, and this row's action_type marks exactly such a change (NEW, UPDCUST, INACT); L1.statement-content requires that statement carry whether the customer is active or inactive. chain/anchors/sources-v1.json states what each code means (NEW, UPDCUST: active; INACT: inactive) with its own cited authority; interpreting that stated meaning to populate this statement's status is reading a named reference the source defines, not inventing a mapping from action codes to status values.
handoff.raw.customer_mgmt_action.action_.parallel_assumption: Credible while the anchored action_type_meanings (assumed authority, locator unverified; see sources-v1.json) correctly and exhaustively state NEW and UPDCUST as active and INACT as inactive for a customer statement; if the business states a different meaning for any of these codes, or a code outside this enumeration is observed, this handoff must be revisited.

handoff.raw.customer_mgmt_action.c_tier-.necessity: L1.statement-content requires a customer's dated statement to carry the customer's tier; this file is where a customer is first recorded or later actioned, and c_tier is the brokerage's own recorded tier value on each such record.
handoff.raw.customer_mgmt_action.c_tier-.parallel_assumption: Credible while c_tier on this file's rows records the tier the brokerage considers the customer to hold as of that row's action_ts.

handoff.raw.customer_mgmt_action.ca_tax_.necessity: L1.statement-content requires an account's dated statement to carry its tax treatment; this file's account actions carry ca_tax_st as the brokerage's own recorded tax-treatment value on each such record.
handoff.raw.customer_mgmt_action.ca_tax_.parallel_assumption: Credible while ca_tax_st on this file's rows records the tax treatment the brokerage considers the account to hold as of that row's action_ts.

inv.account_statement_has_content.necessity: L1.statement-content requires a dated statement to carry the enumerated standing facts, not merely exist as an empty shell; this invariant is the direct check that status and tax_treatment are populated on every candidate-sourced statement, whether supplied directly by the source or carried forward under L1.omitted-facts-stand when the producing action omits the field.
inv.account_statement_has_content.parallel_assumption: Holds unconditionally for statements sourced from the historical action file: NEW, ADDACCT, and UPDACCT carry ca_tax_st directly, and CLOSEACCT omits it, so tax_treatment is carried forward from the account's preceding statement under L1.omitted-facts-stand; status is entailed by the anchored action_type meaning on every one of NEW, ADDACCT, UPDACCT, and CLOSEACCT. Also holds unconditionally for statements sourced from the labeled constructed scenario ce.account_changes, which carries both status_id and tax_status_id directly on every row. Does not yet hold for a statement whose only source is an incremental account change record, since that record's effective moment is not yet resolvable (L1.hole.change-effective-time) and its content handoffs remain deferred.

inv.customer_statement_has_content.necessity: L1.statement-content requires a dated statement to carry the enumerated standing facts, not merely exist as an empty shell; this invariant is the direct check that status and tier are populated on every candidate-sourced statement, whether supplied directly by the source or carried forward under L1.omitted-facts-stand when the producing action omits the field.
inv.customer_statement_has_content.parallel_assumption: Holds unconditionally for statements sourced from the historical action file: NEW and UPDCUST carry c_tier directly, and INACT omits it, so tier is carried forward from the customer's preceding statement under L1.omitted-facts-stand; status is entailed by the anchored action_type meaning on every one of NEW, UPDCUST, and INACT. Does not yet hold for a statement whose only source is an incremental customer change record, since that record's effective moment is not yet resolvable (L1.hole.change-effective-time) and its content handoffs remain deferred.

logical.account.status.necessity: L1.statement-content requires an account's dated statement to carry whether the account is open or closed; this attribute carries that fact directly on the statement.
logical.account.status.parallel_assumption: Credible where the source of this statement supplies its open/closed fact directly, or entails it through a stated code meaning: the historical action file entails it through the anchored meaning of action_type (NEW, ADDACCT, UPDACCT: open; CLOSEACCT: closed), the labeled constructed scenario supplies it directly through status_id, and an incremental account change record supplies it directly through ca_st_id though its effective moment is not yet resolvable (L1.hole.change-effective-time). Whether a CLOSEACCT-derived closed status remains accurate after any later, unrecorded reopening is bounded by L1.hole.closed-account-activity, not resolved by any handoff.

logical.account.tax_treatment.necessity: L1.statement-content requires an account's dated statement to carry its tax treatment; this attribute carries that fact directly on the statement. Where the producing action omits this field (as CLOSEACCT does), this attribute's own carried_forward_from_previous_statement derivation supplies it instead, per L1.omitted-facts-stand, L1.identity, and L1.history.
logical.account.tax_treatment.parallel_assumption: Credible where the source of this statement supplies its own tax-treatment fact directly, or, when the producing action omits it, per the carried-forward derivation; credible while an action's omission of tax treatment is understood to mean the fact is unchanged rather than unknown. The preceding statement this derivation carries from is itself sourced from the historical action file only while incremental account CDC content handoffs stay deferred under L1.hole.change-effective-time; should they be promoted to candidate, this derivation must be revisited for how it identifies the immediately preceding statement.

logical.customer.status.necessity: L1.statement-content requires a customer's dated statement to carry whether the customer is active or inactive; this attribute carries that fact directly on the statement.
logical.customer.status.parallel_assumption: Credible where the source of this statement supplies its active/inactive fact directly, or entails it through a stated code meaning: the historical action file entails it through the anchored meaning of action_type (NEW, UPDCUST: active; INACT: inactive), and an incremental customer change record supplies it directly through c_st_id, though the latter's effective moment is not yet resolvable (L1.hole.change-effective-time).

logical.customer.tier.necessity: L1.statement-content requires a customer's dated statement to carry the customer's tier; this attribute carries that fact directly on the statement. Where the producing action omits this field (as INACT does), this attribute's own carried_forward_from_previous_statement derivation supplies it instead, per L1.omitted-facts-stand, L1.identity, and L1.history.
logical.customer.tier.parallel_assumption: Credible where the source of this statement supplies its own tier fact directly, or, when the producing action omits it, per the carried-forward derivation; credible while an action's omission of tier is understood to mean the fact is unchanged rather than unknown. The preceding statement this derivation carries from is itself sourced from the historical action file only while incremental customer CDC content handoffs stay deferred under L1.hole.change-effective-time; should they be promoted to candidate, this derivation must be revisited for how it identifies the immediately preceding statement.

type.account_standing_status.necessity: L1.statement-content enumerates 'whether the account is open or closed' as part of the standing facts an account's dated statement carries; a dedicated status value is indispensable to express that specific enumerated fact, distinct from tax treatment and ownership.
type.account_standing_status.parallel_assumption: Credible while the brokerage's own status coding distinguishes exactly open and closed states for an account at the moment of a statement.

type.account_tax_treatment.necessity: L1.statement-content enumerates 'its tax treatment' as part of the standing facts an account's dated statement carries; a dedicated tax-treatment value is indispensable to express that specific enumerated fact.
type.account_tax_treatment.parallel_assumption: Credible while the brokerage records a single tax-treatment value per account statement, consistent with a per_statement fact.

type.customer_standing_status.necessity: L1.statement-content enumerates 'whether the customer is active or inactive' as part of the standing facts a customer's dated statement carries; a dedicated status value is indispensable to express that specific enumerated fact, distinct from tier. It belongs to one dated statement and is never replaced in place.
type.customer_standing_status.parallel_assumption: Credible while the brokerage's own status coding distinguishes exactly active and inactive states for a customer at the moment of a statement; a source that reports additional intermediate states would require this type to be reassessed.

type.customer_tier.necessity: L1.statement-content enumerates 'the customer's tier' as part of the standing facts a customer's dated statement carries; a dedicated tier value is indispensable to express that specific enumerated fact.
type.customer_tier.parallel_assumption: Credible while the brokerage records a single tier value per customer statement, consistent with a per_statement fact rather than a running total.

sg.constructed-scenarios.coverage_claim: chain/anchors/sources-v1.json anchors no labeled constructed source for trades (only ce.account_changes exists, and that is for accounts); this job therefore has no handoff that could mix an unlabeled constructed fact into the trade entity, and inv.trade_not_constructed restates that every trade statement this model can produce originates from raw.trade_cdc alone, satisfying L1.constructed-scenarios' labeling and non-mixing requirement vacuously for this job as it stands. Because owning_account_effective_from and owning_customer_number (sg.placement-moment) are references to the upstream account statement, not copies of its facts, a trade whose ownership pins a statement sourced from ce.account_changes carries that statement's own provenance label reachable through the reference; this job introduces no separate, unlabeled copy that could obscure it.

inv.trade_not_constructed.necessity: L1.constructed-scenarios requires a constructed scenario to be labeled wherever it appears and never mixed into received records; with no constructed trade source anchored, this job has no mechanism that could introduce an unlabeled constructed fact into the trade entity, satisfying the clause vacuously for this job as it stands.
inv.trade_not_constructed.parallel_assumption: Credible while sources-v1.json continues to anchor no labeled constructed source for trades; if one is added, this invariant and the model must be revisited.

sg.outcome.coverage_claim: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome enumerates exactly six outcome facts -- status, executed price, fees, commission, tax, quantity -- that change as a trade moves through its life. Each is handed off from raw.trade_cdc's own field for that fact (t_st_id, t_trade_price, t_chrg, t_comm, t_tax, t_qty respectively), typed mutable, and a later CDC row for the same trade_number replaces each with its newly reported value, which inv.trade_outcome_updates_in_place restates directly. All six facts the clause names are covered by a member of this group; the clause names no others.

handoff.raw.trade_cdc.t_chrg->logical.tr.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome requires a later report to update the trade's fees; raw.trade_cdc's t_chrg is the brokerage's own recorded charge value on each report, the fees fact the clause names.
handoff.raw.trade_cdc.t_chrg->logical.tr.parallel_assumption: Credible while t_chrg on a trade_cdc row names the fees the brokerage charges on the trade, as of that report.

handoff.raw.trade_cdc.t_comm->logical.tr.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome requires a later report to update the trade's commission; raw.trade_cdc's t_comm is the brokerage's own recorded commission value on each report.
handoff.raw.trade_cdc.t_comm->logical.tr.parallel_assumption: Credible while t_comm on a trade_cdc row names the commission charged on the trade, as of that report.

handoff.raw.trade_cdc.t_qty->logical.tra.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome requires a later report to update the trade's quantity; raw.trade_cdc's t_qty is the brokerage's own recorded quantity value on each report.
handoff.raw.trade_cdc.t_qty->logical.tra.parallel_assumption: Credible while t_qty on a trade_cdc row names the trade's quantity, as of that report.

handoff.raw.trade_cdc.t_st_id->logical.t.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome requires a later report of a trade to update its status; raw.trade_cdc's t_st_id is the brokerage's own recorded lifecycle-status value on each report of the trade.
handoff.raw.trade_cdc.t_st_id->logical.t.parallel_assumption: Credible while t_st_id on a trade_cdc row names the trade's lifecycle status as of that report.

handoff.raw.trade_cdc.t_tax->logical.tra.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome requires a later report to update the trade's tax; raw.trade_cdc's t_tax is the brokerage's own recorded tax value on each report.
handoff.raw.trade_cdc.t_tax->logical.tra.parallel_assumption: Credible while t_tax on a trade_cdc row names the tax owed on the trade, as of that report.

handoff.raw.trade_cdc.t_trade_price->log.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome requires a later report to update the trade's executed price; raw.trade_cdc's t_trade_price is the brokerage's own recorded executed-price value on each report, distinct from t_bid_price, which records the price at which the trade was requested rather than executed and this job does not hand off.
handoff.raw.trade_cdc.t_trade_price->log.parallel_assumption: Credible while t_trade_price on a trade_cdc row names the price at which the trade actually executed, as of that report.

inv.trade_outcome_updates_in_place.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome states directly that a later report of the same trade updates the outcome; this invariant is the restatement of that update-in-place requirement over the six named outcome facts.
inv.trade_outcome_updates_in_place.parallel_assumption: Holds while every raw.trade_cdc row for a given t_id is a later report about that same trade rather than an unrelated new trade reusing the number.

logical.trade.commission.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome requires a trade's outcome, including its commission, to change as it moves through its life and requires a later report to update that fact; this attribute carries commission directly and is replaced by each later report.
logical.trade.commission.parallel_assumption: Credible while a trade report supplies its own commission fact once determinable; a report of a trade not yet executed may carry no commission value yet, which the clause does not forbid.

logical.trade.executed_price.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome requires a trade's outcome, including its executed price, to change as it moves through its life and requires a later report to update that fact; this attribute carries executed price directly and is replaced by each later report.
logical.trade.executed_price.parallel_assumption: Credible while a trade report supplies its own executed-price fact once the trade has executed; a report of a trade that has not yet executed may carry no executed price yet, which the clause does not forbid.

logical.trade.fees.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome requires a trade's outcome, including its fees, to change as it moves through its life and requires a later report to update that fact; this attribute carries fees directly and is replaced by each later report.
logical.trade.fees.parallel_assumption: Credible while a trade report supplies its own fees fact once determinable; a report of a trade not yet executed may carry no fees value yet, which the clause does not forbid.

logical.trade.quantity.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome requires a trade's outcome, including its quantity, to change as it moves through its life and requires a later report to update that fact; this attribute carries quantity directly and is replaced by each later report.
logical.trade.quantity.parallel_assumption: Credible while every trade report carries a determinable quantity, from the moment it is placed onward.

logical.trade.status.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome requires a trade's outcome, including its status, to change as it moves through its life and requires a later report to update that fact; this attribute carries status directly and is replaced by each later report.
logical.trade.status.parallel_assumption: Credible while every trade report carries a determinable lifecycle status (pending, submitted, completed, or cancelled).

logical.trade.tax.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome requires a trade's outcome, including its tax, to change as it moves through its life and requires a later report to update that fact; this attribute carries tax directly and is replaced by each later report.
logical.trade.tax.parallel_assumption: Credible while a trade report supplies its own tax fact once determinable; a report of a trade not yet executed may carry no tax value yet, which the clause does not forbid.

type.trade_commission.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome names commission as one of the outcome facts that changes through a trade's life; a dedicated value is indispensable to express that specific fact, distinct from fees and tax.
type.trade_commission.parallel_assumption: Credible while the brokerage records a single commission value per trade report, replaced rather than accumulated.

type.trade_executed_price.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome names executed price as one of the outcome facts that changes through a trade's life; a dedicated value is indispensable to express that specific fact, distinct from any bid or requested price.
type.trade_executed_price.parallel_assumption: Credible while the brokerage records a single executed-price value per trade report, replaced rather than accumulated.

type.trade_fees.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome names fees as one of the outcome facts that changes through a trade's life; a dedicated value is indispensable to express that specific fact, distinct from commission and tax.
type.trade_fees.parallel_assumption: Credible while the brokerage records a single fees value per trade report, replaced rather than accumulated.

type.trade_quantity.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome names quantity as one of the outcome facts that changes through a trade's life; a dedicated value is indispensable to express that specific fact.
type.trade_quantity.parallel_assumption: Credible while the brokerage records a single quantity value per trade report, replaced rather than accumulated.

type.trade_status.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome names status as one of the outcome facts that changes as a trade moves through its life (pending, submitted, completed, cancelled); a dedicated value is indispensable to express that fact, replaced by a later report rather than kept beside it.
type.trade_status.parallel_assumption: Credible while the brokerage's own status coding names the trade's current lifecycle stage on every report.

type.trade_tax.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome names tax as one of the outcome facts that changes through a trade's life; a dedicated value is indispensable to express that specific fact, distinct from fees and commission.
type.trade_tax.parallel_assumption: Credible while the brokerage records a single tax value per trade report, replaced rather than accumulated.

sg.placement-moment.coverage_claim: L1.placement-moment fixes placement to the moment stated by the trade's earliest held report, in that report's own time: placed_at, handed off from raw.trade_cdc's t_dts with selector first_encounter_only, carries exactly that moment, frozen. L1.attribution-at-placement requires the trade's ownership to reference the account (and through it the customer) as they stood at that moment, not the account's current statement; L1.as-of defines that answer as the upstream logical.account statement whose effective_from is the latest at or before placed_at. owning_account_effective_from, handed off from logical.account.effective_from with selector as_of_event_time, completes the (account_number, effective_from) pair with owning_account_number (sg.trade-shape) that identifies that exact statement. owning_customer_number is handed off directly from that same pinned statement's own logical.account.owning_customer_number, so it can never name a customer inconsistent with it, satisfying the 'and through it the customer' half of the clause. inv.trade_placement_reference_frozen restates that all three attributes are set once, at first encounter, and never replaced. L1.placement-moment also calls for a first_seen_late marker distinguishing a trade whose first-encountered report is not its true earliest lifecycle report; this job does not derive that marker because sources-v1.json anchors no meaning for raw.trade_cdc's cdc_flag or t_st_id codes that would let this job detect a skipped earlier report without inventing code meanings the anchors do not state -- left as a note on logical.trade rather than modeled or blocked by a question, per this cycle's authority.

handoff.logical.account.effective_from->.necessity: L1.attribution-at-placement requires the trade's ownership reference to name the account as it stood at the moment of placement; L1.as-of defines that answer as the latest statement that took effect at or before the queried moment. This handoff selects, among the upstream ownership-history statements of this trade's owning_account_number, the one whose effective_from is the latest at or before placed_at, and freezes that effective_from as the second half of the (account_number, effective_from) reference identifying the specific account statement -- not the account's current statement.
handoff.logical.account.effective_from->.parallel_assumption: Credible while the upstream logical.account entity carries a resolvable statement of this trade's owning account with an effective_from at or before placed_at.

handoff.logical.account.owning_customer_.necessity: L1.attribution-at-placement requires that, through the account, the trade also belongs to the customer as that customer stood at the same moment; the account statement already pinned by owning_account_number and owning_account_effective_from carries, as its own owning_customer_number, exactly that customer. This handoff freezes that same value directly off the pinned statement rather than performing an independent as-of lookup, so the customer named can never be inconsistent with the account statement this trade's ownership pins.
handoff.logical.account.owning_customer_.parallel_assumption: Credible wherever the account statement pinned by owning_account_number and owning_account_effective_from itself has a resolvable owning_customer_number.

handoff.raw.trade_cdc.t_dts->logical.tra.necessity: L1.placement-moment requires placement to be the moment stated by the earliest report of the trade the brokerage holds, in that report's own time; raw.trade_cdc's t_dts is that report's own recorded time, and this handoff takes it only from the trade's first-encountered report, never a later one.
handoff.raw.trade_cdc.t_dts->logical.tra.parallel_assumption: Credible while t_dts on a trade's first-encountered report is the report's own stated time of that event, not a receipt or batch-load time.

inv.trade_placement_reference_frozen.necessity: L1.placement-moment fixes placement to the earliest held report's own time, and L1.attribution-at-placement states directly that later changes do not move a trade that was already placed; this invariant is the restatement of that requirement over the placement-moment reference attributes.
inv.trade_placement_reference_frozen.parallel_assumption: Holds while a later raw.trade_cdc report of a known trade never carries an earlier event time than the one already recorded as placed_at.

logical.trade.owning_account_effective_f.necessity: L1.attribution-at-placement requires the account to be referenced as it stood at placement, not merely named; together with owning_account_number, this attribute completes the (account_number, effective_from) pair that identifies the specific account statement in effect at placed_at, per L1.as-of's 'latest statement that took effect at or before' the queried moment.
logical.trade.owning_account_effective_f.parallel_assumption: Credible while the upstream logical.account entity carries a statement of this trade's owning account with an effective_from at or before placed_at; not yet resolvable where the correct statement is one of ownership-history's own deferred CDC-sourced account statements.

logical.trade.owning_customer_number.necessity: L1.attribution-at-placement requires that, through the account, the trade also belongs to the customer as that customer stood at the same moment; this attribute carries that customer directly from the same account statement owning_account_number and owning_account_effective_from already pin, so it can never name a customer inconsistent with that statement.
logical.trade.owning_customer_number.parallel_assumption: Credible while the account statement pinned by owning_account_number and owning_account_effective_from has a resolvable owning_customer_number.

logical.trade.placed_at.necessity: L1.placement-moment requires placement to be the moment stated by the earliest report of the trade the brokerage holds, in that report's own time; this attribute carries that moment, set once at first encounter and never replaced by a later report.
logical.trade.placed_at.parallel_assumption: Credible while the trade's first-encountered report states its own event time.

type.trade_owning_account_effective_from.necessity: L1.attribution-at-placement requires the trade's ownership to reference the account as it stood at placement, not merely which account; L1.as-of defines that answer as the account's statement whose effective_from is the latest at or before the queried moment; a dedicated value carrying that specific effective_from is required to complete the (account_number, effective_from) reference that identifies the exact account statement. L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome states directly that a later report of the same trade 'leaves the ownership as first recorded'; on this entity (incremental_by_identity, not versioned), that reference is fixed once at first encounter and never replaced by a later report, which is exactly the frozen_from_first_encounter role -- not per_statement, which describes a value's own kept-history nature on a versioned entity, a role that belongs to the account entity this value is drawn from, not to how it behaves once pinned here.
type.trade_owning_account_effective_from.parallel_assumption: Credible while the upstream logical.account entity carries a statement of this trade's owning account whose effective_from is at or before placed_at.

type.trade_owning_customer_reference.necessity: L1.attribution-at-placement requires that, through the account, the trade also belongs to the customer as that customer stood at the same moment; a dedicated value naming that customer is required to express that half of the clause. L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome states directly that a later report of the same trade 'leaves the ownership as first recorded'; on this entity (incremental_by_identity, not versioned), that customer reference is fixed once at first encounter and never replaced by a later report, which is exactly the frozen_from_first_encounter role -- not per_statement, which describes the value's own kept-history nature on the account entity it is drawn from, not how it behaves once pinned here.
type.trade_owning_customer_reference.parallel_assumption: Credible while the account statement this trade's ownership pins has a resolvable owning customer.

type.trade_placed_at.necessity: L1.placement-moment requires the trade's placement to be the moment stated by the earliest report of it the brokerage holds, in that report's own recorded time. L1.attribution-at-placement requires that a later change does not move a trade that was already placed; since this moment is what selects the account statement the trade references, it must be set once and never replaced, or a later report could shift which statement is selected and move the trade's ownership.
type.trade_placed_at.parallel_assumption: Credible while the earliest report of a trade the brokerage holds states its own time, and that time is treated as the placement moment even when it is not the trade's true first lifecycle event (the first-seen-late case L1.placement-moment names).

sg.trade-identity.coverage_claim: Every raw.trade_cdc row carries t_id, the brokerage's own trade number, handed off unchanged into trade_number with the identity mutation role; because this value is identical across every CDC row reporting the same trade, no later report ever produces a 'different' trade, satisfying L1.identity's persistence requirement for the trade entity.

handoff.raw.trade_cdc.t_id->logical.trad.necessity: L1.identity requires the trade's own number as its identity; raw.trade_cdc carries t_id as the brokerage's trade number on every row reporting that trade, including its first-encountered row and every later report.
handoff.raw.trade_cdc.t_id->logical.trad.parallel_assumption: Credible while t_id values in this file are the brokerage's real trade numbers and not reused for different trades.

logical.trade.trade_number.necessity: L1.identity requires a value that identifies which trade a report is about and stays the same across every later report of that trade; this attribute carries the identity type for exactly that purpose.
logical.trade.trade_number.parallel_assumption: Credible while the brokerage's trade number is stable and unique per trade.

type.trade_number.necessity: L1.identity requires that a change to a trade does not make it a different trade; a value invariant across every report of the same trade is required to express that persistence, which is exactly the identity mutation role.
type.trade_number.parallel_assumption: Credible while the brokerage's trade number is never reassigned to a different trade; if a trade number were reused for a different trade this role would misidentify reports, which should trigger review.

sg.trade-shape.coverage_claim: logical.trade's history kind, incremental_by_identity, is the direct consequence of L1.identity (a trade is a persistent identified thing; a later report about the same trade number is the same trade, not a new one), L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome (a later report updates outcome facts on this same row), and L1.attribution-at-placement (the trade's ownership, once established at placement, is never moved by a later report about the account or customer) -- together these entail one row per trade_number, updated in place, holding a frozen portion beside a mutable portion. The frozen portion's account-identity component is owning_account_number: raw.trade_cdc's t_ca_id, taken only from the trade's first-encountered report and never replaced by a later one, which inv.trade_owning_account_frozen restates directly. This is the part of L1.attribution-at-placement that names which account a trade belongs to, fixed at first encounter; the remaining part -- which dated statement of that account, and through it which customer, stood as of the moment of placement -- is now resolved by L1.placement-moment and covered by sg.placement-moment instead, since that is the more specific claim. This group's own scope is limited to the entity's shape and the account-identity portion.

handoff.raw.trade_cdc.t_ca_id->logical.t.necessity: L1.attribution-at-placement requires the trade's own account be named and fixed at first encounter; raw.trade_cdc's t_ca_id is the brokerage's own recorded account number on the trade's first-encountered report, and this handoff takes that value only, never a later report's t_ca_id, per the clause's 'do not move a trade that was already placed.'
handoff.raw.trade_cdc.t_ca_id->logical.t.parallel_assumption: Credible while t_ca_id on a trade's first-encountered report names the account the trade was placed under.

inv.trade_owning_account_frozen.necessity: L1.attribution-at-placement states directly that later changes do not move a trade that was already placed; this invariant is the restatement of that requirement over the account a trade is recorded against.
inv.trade_owning_account_frozen.parallel_assumption: Holds while raw.trade_cdc never legitimately reassigns a trade to a different account after its first report; a contradiction would indicate a data error or an unaddressed business rule, not a value this attribute should adopt.

logical.trade.necessity: L1.identity requires a trade to be the same persistent identified thing across every report of it, not a new trade each time. L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome requires that a later report of the same trade update its outcome (status, executed price, fees, commission, tax, quantity) in place. L1.attribution-at-placement requires that a trade's ownership, once established at placement, is never moved by a later change to the account or customer, and that nothing the trade created is moved either. Together these entail exactly one row per identified trade, updated in place by later reports, holding a portion frozen at first encounter beside a portion that mutates -- the incremental_by_identity history kind, not versioned (which would keep every report as a separate dated statement) and not append_by_identity (which would treat every report as a new, unrelated event).
logical.trade.parallel_assumption: Credible while every raw.trade_cdc row for the same t_id is understood to be a later report about that same trade rather than a distinct trade reusing the number.

logical.trade.owning_account_number.necessity: L1.attribution-at-placement requires a trade to belong to the account it was placed under and forbids a later change from moving it; this attribute names that account, set once at first encounter and never replaced by a later report.
logical.trade.owning_account_number.parallel_assumption: Credible while the account a trade is placed under is settled at the trade's first-encountered report; whether a later report could legitimately correct it is not addressed by the clause and is not assumed here.

type.trade_owning_account_reference.necessity: L1.attribution-at-placement requires a trade to belong to the account it was placed under, and requires that a later change does not move a trade that was already placed; a value naming that account, set once and never replaced by a later report, is required to express that. L1.identity supplies the account's own persistent number as the value this reference carries.
type.trade_owning_account_reference.parallel_assumption: Credible while a trade's account assignment is settled at the trade's first-encountered report and never legitimately contradicted by a later report of the same trade.

clauses.L1.as-of: Any question about a customer or account can be asked as of a moment in time, and the answer is the statement in effect at that moment: the latest one that took effect at or before it.
clauses.L1.attribution-at-placement: A trade belongs to the account, and through it the customer, as they stood at the moment the trade was placed. Later changes to that account or customer do not move a trade that was already placed, and do not move anything that trade created.
clauses.L1.constructed-scenarios: Any scenario built to test these rules, rather than received from the brokerage's records, is labeled as constructed wherever it appears and is never mixed into the received records. A constructed scenario changes something the received records already know; it never introduces a customer, account, or trade the brokerage does not have. (Second sentence is an authorized clarification, assumed under `issue-8-statement-content-assumed`; review trigger: business confirmation.)
clauses.L1.current-version: The current statement about a customer or account is the one with no later statement. There is exactly one current statement per customer and per account.
clauses.L1.history: Every change to a customer or an account is kept, with the moment it took effect. Nothing about a customer or account is overwritten; a later statement sits beside the earlier one.
clauses.L1.holdings-follow-trade: A change in what an account holds is caused by a trade. The holding change belongs to whoever owned the trade that caused it, as that trade's ownership was recorded. Holdings are never re-attributed by looking the account up again later.
clauses.L1.identity: Customers, accounts, and trades are the things the brokerage already identifies: a customer number, an account number, a trade number. A change to a customer or an account does not make it a different customer or account; it makes a new dated statement about the same one.
clauses.L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome: As a trade moves through its life (pending, submitted, completed, cancelled), its outcome changes: status, executed price, fees, commission, tax, quantity. Its ownership does not change. A later report of the same trade updates the outcome and leaves the ownership as first recorded.
clauses.L1.no-phantom-positions: Summing holding changes for any one statement of an account or customer can never go below zero. A negative result means a holding was opened under one statement and closed under another, which the clauses above forbid.
clauses.L1.omitted-facts-stand: A change that does not mention a standing fact leaves that fact as it last stood. A statement produced by such a change carries the fact at its last stated value. (Assumed under `issue-8-statement-content-assumed`; review trigger: the business confirms or amends.)
clauses.L1.owner-standing: An account's standing includes its owner's standing. When the brokerage says how an account stood at a moment, that includes how its customer stood at that same moment.
clauses.L1.placement-moment: A trade is placed at the moment of the earliest report of it the brokerage holds, as that report states its own time. A later report of a trade the brokerage has not seen before is treated as its placement and marked as first seen late, so the ownership it fixes can be reviewed. (Assumed under `issue-8-statement-content-assumed`; review trigger: the business confirms or amends.)
clauses.L1.statement-content: A dated statement carries the brokerage's standing facts at that moment. For a customer: whether the customer is active or inactive, and the customer's tier. For an account: whether the account is open or closed, its tax treatment, and which customer owns it. Names, addresses, contact details, and tax identifiers are not part of standing until a job needs them. (Assumed under `issue-8-statement-content-assumed`; review trigger: the business confirms or amends this enumeration.)

holes.L1.hole.batch-identity: Does a report need to know which incremental file first delivered a fact?
holes.L1.hole.change-effective-time: Incremental change files carry no time of their own. Does a change in such a file take effect at the file's batch date, or at some other moment?
holes.L1.hole.closed-account-activity: Trades appear on accounts the brokerage recorded as closed years earlier (account 428 closed in 2012, trades in 2017). Is that a data error, a reopening the records omit, or does a closed account still own trades?
holes.L1.hole.deletions: Incremental files can mark a record deleted. What does deleting a trade or account mean for history, ownership, and holdings?
holes.L1.hole.owner-change-reversions-account: When a customer's standing changes, does the brokerage consider every account of that customer to have a new statement at that moment, or only the customer? The source data shows customer changes without matching account changes.
holes.L1.hole.securities-and-brokers: Securities, companies, and brokers are named in the records but not yet part of any job. When they are, the attribution rule must be restated for them.
holes.L1.hole.trade-timestamps: Which moment counts as "when it completed" when a later report of a trade arrives without its full history? (Placement is settled, provisionally, by `L1.placement-moment`.)

ownership-history.description: Know how any customer or account stood at any moment, and who owned what.
ownership-history.feedback: one current statement per customer and per account; statements of one thing do not overlap; any as-of question has exactly one answer with the standing facts of L1.statement-content; an account's as-of answer carries its customer's as-of answer

positions.description: Know what each account and customer holds, and how it got there.
positions.feedback: every holding change carries the ownership recorded on its causing trade; no statement of an account or customer sums below zero

trade-lifecycle.description: Know each trade's outcome and who owned it when it happened.
trade-lifecycle.feedback: a later report of a trade changes its outcome fields and leaves its recorded ownership byte-identical; ownership equals the account's as-of statement at placement, not the current one; placement is the earliest held report's own time
